Q: How can Apache Camel be used to monitor file changes? A:

You can do this by setting up the idempotentKey to tell Camel how a file is considered changed. For example if the file size changes, or its timestamp changes etc.

See more details at the Camel file documentation at: https://camel.apache.org/components/latest/file-component.html

See the section Avoiding reading the same file more than once (idempotent consumer). And read about idempotent and idempotentKey.

So something alike

from("file:/somedir?noop=true&idempotentKey=${file:name}-${file:size}")

Or

from("file:/somedir?noop=true&idempotentKey=${file:name}-${file:modified}")

You can read here about the various ${file:xxx} tokens you can use: http://camel.apache.org/file-language.html

Q: Use CSS to hide elements by class name dependent on body element attribute A:

Fair pushback, but it depends heavily on context. If this is an internal app or SPA-like UI (editors, dashboards), avoiding round-trips and toggling visibility client-side is completely reasonable—SEO and initial payload aren’t primary concerns there.

The real issue isn’t “CSS vs JS”, it’s render strategy: sending all modes upfront trades bandwidth for latency. At ~100kb and no heavy assets, that’s negligible, but it doesn’t scale if modes grow complex.

A cleaner middle ground is lazy rendering (load or mount panels only when needed) rather than preloading everything and hiding 75% of it.

Q: SQL - Get Min, Max date for a given group with break in dates A:

https://sqlfiddle.com/oracle/online-compiler?&id=7ae92964-0155-4d3b-88a3-d9e741d68084

This is a common island and gaps problem, by creating a sequence and row number within each group we calculate the difference between these giving us a grouping to use.

WITH CTE AS (SELECT id,cd, p_dt, value,i_dt
 , row_number() over (order by p_dt) -
    row_number() over (partition by id, cd, value order by p_dt) as grp
            FROM T)

SELECT id,cd,value,min(p_dt) minP_dt, max(p_dt) maxP_dt,  grp
FROM CTE
group by id,cd,value,  grp
Order by value, minP_dt;

Giving us:

`+----+----+-------+-----------+-----------+-----+`
`| ID | CD | VALUE |  MINP_DT  |  MAXP_DT  | GRP |`
`+----+----+-------+-----------+-----------+-----+`
`|  1 | A  |     9 | 12-JAN-12 | 16-JAN-12 |   2 |`
`|  1 | A  |    10 | 10-JAN-12 | 11-JAN-12 |   0 |`
`|  1 | A  |    10 | 17-JAN-12 | 18-JAN-12 |   3 |`
`+----+----+-------+-----------+-----------+-----+`

Q: Modify the StatusHandlers in DefaultRestClientBuilder? A:

You can’t modify the list directly—StatusHandler is intentionally package-private, so Spring only allows adding, not mutating/removing.
Treat it as an append-only pipeline and control behavior via predicates and ordering.

builder
  .defaultStatusHandler(HttpStatusCode::is4xxClientError, (req,res)->{/*...*/})
  .defaultStatusHandler(HttpStatusCode::is5xxServerError, (req,res)->{/*...*/});
